name: stripe-type
title: Stripe Type
description: A word cut into horizontal bands, as in the IBM logo, slides together from alternating sides and locks, then can pass on through.
useWhen: A bold word needs a graphic, engineered entrance on a flat field, such as a product name or a section title.
You want the striped-logo look as the resting state, or as a transition into solid type with Settle set to solid.
A word should enter and leave in one move: the bands arrive from alternating sides and exit through the other.
avoidWhen: The word should split along its letters rather than in horizontal bands: use typed-split-wipe.
The whole frame should fill with moving rows of type: use type-wall.
A soft, quiet entrance fits better: use mask-reveal-up.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Settle
variables.description: Resting look once the bands lock.

variables.label: Font size
variables.description: Text size in reference pixels (720 high stage); long words shrink to fit.

variables.label: Gap
variables.description: Share of each pitch left empty between bands.

variables.label: Hold
variables.description: Frames the word rests before leaving (30 fps). The clip is sized for 30.

variables.label: Exit
variables.description: Bands leave through the opposite side.
